questions.question: When did Elizabeth I's reign as Queen of England and Ireland begin?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states she was queen from 17 November 1558 until her death in 1603.
Incorrect. 7 September 1533 is Elizabeth's birth date, not the start of her reign.
Incorrect. 24 March 1603 is Elizabeth's death date, marking the end of her reign.
Incorrect. 1547 is the year Henry VIII died, not when Elizabeth began her reign.

questions.question: Who were Elizabeth I's parents?
options: Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon
answer_explanations: Correct. The article identifies Elizabeth as the only surviving child of Henry VIII and his second wife, Anne Boleyn.
Incorrect. Catherine of Aragon was Henry VIII's first wife and Mary I's mother, not Elizabeth's mother.
Incorrect. Edward VI and Mary I were Elizabeth's half-siblings, not her parents.
Incorrect. William Cecil and Francis Walsingham were advisers and ministers, not Elizabeth's parents.

questions.question: What happened to Elizabeth's mother, Anne Boleyn, when Elizabeth was two years old?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that when Elizabeth was two years old, her mother was executed.
Incorrect. Anne Boleyn was executed, not made queen regnant.
Incorrect. The article does not say Anne Boleyn fled to France.
Incorrect. The article does not say Anne Boleyn remarried.

questions.question: What nickname is Elizabeth I sometimes given because she never married?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that because Elizabeth never married, she is sometimes referred to as the "Virgin Queen".
Incorrect. "Iron Queen" is not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. "Bloody Mary" refers to Mary I, not Elizabeth I.
Incorrect. "Sun Queen" is not mentioned in the article.

questions.question: Who succeeded Elizabeth I after her death in 1603?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Elizabeth was succeeded by her first cousin twice removed, James VI of Scotland.
Incorrect. Mary I was Elizabeth's half-sister and predecessor, not successor.
Incorrect. Edward VI was Elizabeth's half-brother and predecessor, not successor.
Incorrect. Lady Jane Grey was a Protestant cousin whom Edward VI tried to name as heir, not Elizabeth's successor.

questions.question: What was one of Elizabeth I's mottoes?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article lists one of Elizabeth's mottoes as video et taceo ('I see and keep silent').
Incorrect. "sic semper tyrannis" is not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. "carpe diem" is not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. "veni vidi vici" is not mentioned in the article.

questions.question: Which English monarch ruled immediately before Elizabeth I?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that upon Mary's death in 1558, Elizabeth succeeded to the throne.
Incorrect. Henry VIII was Elizabeth's father and ruled before Edward VI and Mary I.
Incorrect. Edward VI ruled before Mary I, not immediately before Elizabeth.
Incorrect. James VI of Scotland succeeded Elizabeth, he did not rule before her.

questions.question: Where was Elizabeth I born?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Elizabeth was born on 7 September 1533 at Greenwich Palace.
Incorrect. The Tower of London was where Elizabeth was imprisoned during Mary's reign, not where she was born.
Incorrect. Hatfield House is where Elizabeth lived during Seymour's arrest, not her birthplace.
Incorrect. Woodstock Palace is where Elizabeth was held under house arrest, not her birthplace.

questions.question: How long was Elizabeth I imprisoned during Mary's reign?
options: almost a year under house arrest
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that during Mary's reign, Elizabeth was imprisoned for nearly a year on suspicion of supporting Protestant rebels.
Incorrect. Nine days refers to how long Lady Jane Grey was queen before being deposed.
Incorrect. Almost a year under house arrest refers to Elizabeth's time at Woodstock Palace after being moved from the Tower, not her initial imprisonment.
Incorrect. Two years is not mentioned as the length of Elizabeth's imprisonment.

questions.question: What religious arrangement did Elizabeth I establish as one of her first actions as queen?
options: an English church of which she became supreme governor
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states one of her first actions was the establishment of an English church, of which she became the supreme governor, later named the Elizabethan Religious Settlement.
Incorrect. The article does not say Elizabeth returned to papal authority; the pope later declared her illegitimate.
Incorrect. A Lutheran state church is not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. A Calvinist presbyterian system is not mentioned in the article.
